 THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 15.09.2015 PASSED IN MVC NO.1034/2013 ON THE FILE OF THE 2ND ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT-VI, AT DAVANAGERE, AWARDING COMPENSATION OF RS.50,000/-
WITH INTEREST @ 6% P.A FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL REALIZATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the insurance company has challenged the judgment dated 15.09.2015 in MVC No.1034/2013 passed by the 2nd Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT-VI, Davanagere in awarding global compensation of Rs.50,000/- to the petitioner.
2. The parties will be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 22.04.2013 at 12.00 p.m., the petitioner while riding the motorcycle bearing No.KA17-S-7469 along with one Mallikarjunaiah as pillion rider at N.H.4 near NC:
2023:KHC:41431 Anagodu Bus Stand was hit by Mahindra Xylo bearing No.KA17-B-1045 killing Mallikarjunaiah at the spot and injuring the petitioner.
The petitioner who sustained facial injuries has taken treatment at C.J.Hospital, Davanagere and Bapuji Hospital, Davanagere and moved the tribunal for grant of compensation.
Claim was opposed by the respondents.

The tribunal after taking evidence, by impugned common judgment awarded global compensation of Rs.50,000/- with 6%
interest.
Aggrieved by the same, the insurance company has preferred this appeal on various grounds.

4. Heard the argument of Sri.K.Suresh, learned counsel for the insurance company,
Sri.R.Shashidhara, learned counsel for the petitioner.
5.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the insurance company that plea of contributory negligence is not considered by the Tribunal, the petitioner has sustained simple injuries and even if NC: 2023:KHC:41431 the medical expenses is considered, the compensation will not exceed more than Rs.25,000/- and sought for reduction of Rs.25,000/-, award of global compensation is without The Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd vs Sri Revanasiddaiah on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92169812/
2 reasoning and sought for interference.

sentences.text: 6. Per contra, learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that the appeal filed by the insurance company challenging the judgment award in MVC.No.1033/2013, was dismissed by this Court in MFA.No.1228/2016 and there is no question of contributory negligence to be considered and only the quantum of compensation has to be determined.
It is his contention that the petitioner has suffered facial injuries, he was aged 53 years, he was hospitalization for eight days, he was attended by an attendant.

Money spent towards incidental expenses and loss of income during the laid up has been considered by the Tribunal, however he sought for NC: 2023:KHC:41431 enhancement of compensation while supporting the impugned judgment.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both the parties and perused the materials on record.
8. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of the accident, injury sustained by the petitioner and his entitlement to claim the compensation.
Ex.P.12 is the injury certificate pointing out lacerated injury suffered by the petitioner on his left upper eyelid, abrasions over both the eyebrows and knees and was hospitalized for eight days.
The CT Scan opinion points out that the petitioner has suffered sub-arachnoids hemorrhage and interhemispheric fissure.
The medical officer who issued the injury certificate has not given his opinion.

Having regard to the nature of injuries, the injury particularly to left upper high lid and abrasions over the both the eyebrows and NC: 2023:KHC:41431 knees, it is proper to assess the compensation Rs.10,000/- towards pain and sufferings, Rs.12,500/- towards medical expenses, attendant charges of Rs.2000/-, travelling expenses at Rs.2,000/-, food and nourishment Rs.5,000/-, 'loss of income during the laid up period' Rs.8000/-, it comes to Rs.39,500/- rounded of to Rs.40,000/-.
Even under different heads, compensation will not exceed more than Rs.40,000/-.
Hence, the global compensation cannot be sustained and the petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.40,000/-.
Accordingly, the appeal deserves merits consideration.

In the result, the following:
ORDER I. Appeal is allowed in part.
II. The judgment and award modified.

III.
Petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.40,000/- instead of Rs.50,000/-
 NC: 2023:KHC:41431  with 6% interest from the date of  petition till the date of realize  IV.
The amount in deposit shall be  transmitted to the Tribunal.

V. The insurance company is directed to  deposit the compensation within The Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd vs Sri Revanasiddaiah on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92169812/
3 eight weeks from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this judgment.
Sd/-
